After a two-year pause, Apple is developing a new iMac with an M6 chip and updated colour options, expected to launch by the end of this year, according to Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman.

The iMac's update cycle has never been particularly frequent — it skipped the M2 and M5 chip generations, and still does not offer a larger screen option. Apple has instead steered high-end users toward pairing a Mac Studio or Mac mini with a Studio Display. Even so, Apple is preparing a new version with an M6 chip.

Gurman notes that this update will come with "some new colour options," but offers no specific details. Apple already made subtle adjustments to the colour lineup with the 2024 M4 refresh, though the actual seven-colour selection remained unchanged — only the shades shifted slightly. The new iMac is also expected to arrive before the end of the year:

This autumn could be a significant season for the Mac. Expect a heavily redesigned MacBook Pro with a touch screen and Tandem OLED, a new entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro with an M6 chip, new M5 Max and M5 Ultra Mac Studios (subject to supply), and a new iMac with an M6 chip. Another possibility is a new Mac mini with M6 and M5 Pro chips, though that model may arrive a little later.

Apple's M6 chip will be the first Mac chip built on an all-new 2nm process, but there reportedly won't be M6 Pro, M6 Max, or M6 Ultra variants — Apple is said to be accelerating the rollout of the M7 series instead.
